name: Norfolk
description: Norfolk is a largely rural county in eastern England, famous for its flat agricultural landscapes, Norfolk Broads and extensive coastline. Norwich is the principal city, while coastal resorts and historic market towns contribute to a strong tourism and heritage economy.

places.name: Breckland
places.description: A rural district in Norfolk named for the Brecks, a distinctive sandy heathland landscape, and home to the market town of Thetford.

places.name: Broadland
places.description: A district in Norfolk taking in part of the Norfolk Broads, a network of navigable rivers and lakes popular for boating holidays, just north of Norwich.

places.name: Great Yarmouth
places.description: A traditional English seaside resort on the Norfolk coast, once a major herring fishing port, now known for its beach, pier, and Victorian promenade.

places.name: King's Lynn and West Norfolk
places.description: A district centred on the historic Hanseatic League port of King's Lynn, with a well-preserved medieval merchant quarter and the nearby royal Sandringham Estate.

places.name: North Norfolk
places.description: A coastal district in Norfolk known for its salt marshes, seal colonies, and genteel seaside towns like Cromer and Wells-next-the-Sea.

places.name: Norwich
places.description: A historic cathedral city in Norfolk, one of medieval England's largest and wealthiest, with a Norman cathedral, castle, and a distinctive circular market dating back centuries.

places.name: South Norfolk
places.description: A rural district ringing Norwich, covering market towns like Wymondham with its twin-towered abbey church.
